nodes.description: The files in a folder whose names match the pattern (*.png, *.jpg: * and ?, case ignored; several separated by commas), sorted, optionally in its subfolders too. Wire it into a node's file input to run that node once per file, each result labelled with the file's name.

inputs.name: folder
inputs.tooltip: The folder to search

inputs.name: pattern
inputs.tooltip: File names to match: * and ?, several separated by commas (*.png, *.jpg)

inputs.name: recursive
inputs.tooltip: Search the subfolders too

nodes.description: Read a file into a value: an image, an SVG, a PDF or any bytes, its media type from its extension. Given a list of files (Find Files, Select Files), it reads each, so wiring its value into, say, an app's Open image input opens every file.

inputs.name: file
inputs.tooltip: The file to read; wire Find Files or Select Files to read each

nodes.description: The files chosen with … (several at once), as a list: wire it into a node's file input to run that node once per file, each result labelled with the file's name.

inputs.name: files
inputs.tooltip: The files, one path per line: choose them with …

nodes.description: Write values into a folder: each file is named from basename and what made the value (trace_corgi_colors-8.svg: the file it came from and the settings varied), with its type's extension. A different file already there is an error unless overwrite is on.

inputs.name: values
inputs.tooltip: The values to write: one, or a list

inputs.name: folder
inputs.tooltip: The folder to write into (made when missing)

inputs.name: basename
inputs.tooltip: The start of every file name; what varied follows it

inputs.name: overwrite
inputs.tooltip: Replace files that are already there

nodes.description: Where two pictures of one size differ, and by how much.
One channel as a mask, each pixel against its neighbourhood's mean less `offset`: survives uneven lighting.
Two pictures of one size mixed: a × weight a + b × weight b + offset.
Smooths flat areas and keeps edges. Two pixels mix when they are near each other and near in colour.
Masks combined bit by bit, or a picture kept where a mask is set (And with b the same picture). `not` uses only a.
Each pixel the plain mean of its neighbours: the fastest blur.

inputs.name: size
inputs.tooltip: Kernel size; an even one becomes the next odd one

nodes.description: Thin edges as a mask, 0 or 1. Thresholds are 0-1 where OpenCV's are 0-255. A low above the high swaps with it.
A drawing from a photo: flattened colour with dark outlines. `examples/cartoon.json` is the same steps as a group you can open and change.

inputs.name: levels
inputs.tooltip: Pyramid levels: more is flatter and faster

inputs.name: smoothing
inputs.tooltip: Bilateral passes

inputs.name: outline
inputs.tooltip: Adaptive threshold's neighbourhood: larger gives bolder outlines

nodes.description: Equalize Histogram by region, limited so noise isn't amplified: brings out detail in dark and bright areas alike.

inputs.name: limit
inputs.tooltip: How far contrast may rise; lower is gentler

nodes.description: Number each separate shape in a mask: integer labels, 0 for background (the viewer's labels view colours them), and how many.
Contrast and brightness: each value times gain, plus offset, clipped to 0-1.
A rectangle of a picture. One reaching past the edge is cut there; one entirely outside is a config error.
A picture file's bytes, from Encode Image or another engine, as RGB, 0-1. The inverse of Encode Image.
Fast Non-Local Means: removes noise by averaging similar patches. Slow on large pictures, and it can't stop part way once started.
Brings out fine detail, for a crisper picture.
For each set pixel of a mask, how far it is, in pixels, to the nearest unset one.
The contours from Find Contours drawn on a picture. Thickness 0 is taken as 1.

inputs.name: thickness
inputs.tooltip: -1 fills them

nodes.description: A table of x, y drawn on a picture as circles.
A table of x1, y1, x2, y2 drawn on a picture.
Smooths while keeping edges, faster than the bilateral filter.
A picture as a file's bytes, 8 bits a channel, for Write Files or another engine. The inverse of Decode Image.
Spread a picture's tones across the range: one channel directly, RGB by its luminance, so colours keep their hue.
Any convolution, from a kernel you type. The default sharpens.

inputs.name: kernel
inputs.tooltip: Numbers by row, rows split by ;

inputs.name: normalise
inputs.tooltip: Divide by the kernel's sum, when that isn't 0

nodes.description: The outlines of shapes in a mask, as a table: area, perimeter, box, and points as text `x,y x,y …`. Draw Contours puts them back.
A picture mirrored. A second flip undoes it.
A picture in another colour space, back to RGB. The inverse of To Colour Space.
A soft blur. The kernel follows from sigma.
Strong corners, as a table x, y. Draw Points puts them back on a picture.
Separate a subject from its background, given a box around it: a mask, 1 for the subject.

inputs.name: left
inputs.tooltip: The box around the subject, as fractions of the picture

inputs.name: seed
inputs.tooltip: The same seed gives the same result

nodes.description: Straight line segments in an edge mask, as a table x1, y1, x2, y2, length. Draw Segments puts them back on a picture.

inputs.name: edges
inputs.tooltip: An edge mask, from Canny

nodes.description: A mask, 1 where every channel lies in its range. Pairs with To Colour Space, to pick a hue (0-360 in HSV). One channel uses the first range.
Fill a masked area from what surrounds it, to remove a mark or an object.

inputs.name: mask
inputs.tooltip: What to fill: any array above 0, as Threshold or In Range make

nodes.description: A picture reduced to a few colours, and those colours as a table.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.tooltip: The same seed gives the same result

nodes.description: Second derivative: edges as signed values on zero. A value view of `heat` shows them well.
A picture file as RGB, 0-1. A grey file comes as three equal channels.
Each pixel the median of its neighbours: removes specks and keeps edges.

inputs.name: size
inputs.tooltip: Kernel size; an even one becomes the next odd one

nodes.description: Three one-channel arrays of one size as an RGB picture. The inverse of Split Channels.
Grow, shrink or tidy shapes in a mask or picture. Open removes specks; close fills holes.

inputs.name: size
inputs.tooltip: Kernel size; an even one becomes the next odd one

nodes.description: A picture stretched to fill 0-1. A flat picture becomes zeros.
Distinctive points that survive scale and rotation, as a table x, y, size, angle, response. Draw Points puts them back.
A pencil drawing, in grey and in colour.
Half the size, blurred first. Pyramid Up goes back in size, though the detail is gone.
Twice the size, smoothed. Pyramid Down goes back.
A picture at another size. Area suits shrinking, and cubic or Lanczos enlarging.

inputs.name: height
inputs.tooltip: 0 keeps the shape

nodes.description: A picture turned by quarter turns, nothing lost. Three of one turn, or one of the opposite, undo it.
A sharper-angled Sobel, size 3: signed values on zero.
Passes its input through after `seconds`, reporting progress and stopping on cancel. How a long node behaves.
First derivative along one direction: signed values on zero.
Three channels as three arrays. The inverse of Merge Channels.
The shape Morphology uses, 0 and 1, to look at. Also usable as a mask.

inputs.name: size
inputs.tooltip: Kernel size; an even one becomes the next odd one

nodes.description: A painted look: smooth regions with strong edges.
A source with no file: a colour gradient, a disc and a bar, with edges for the other nodes to find.
One channel as a mask, 0 or 1. Otsu and triangle find the level themselves, and level is then ignored.
An RGB picture as one channel of luminance. Colour can't be recovered, so it has no inverse.
RGB in another colour space, in OpenCV's float units: HSV hue 0-360, Lab L 0-100. The inverse of From Colour Space.
One frame of a video file, as RGB, 0-1. Past the end is an op error.
Rotate about the centre, scale and shift, keeping the size; the corners repeat the edge. The opposite angle undoes the rotation, softened.
Grow labelled seeds across a picture until they meet: integer labels, with -1 on the boundaries.

inputs.name: markers
inputs.tooltip: Integer labels, from Connected Components: each seed grows; 0 is unknown

nodes.description: Every combination of the items of a, b (and c), as one list of tuples, the first varying slowest. A single value goes with every item. Unzip splits the tuples again.

inputs.name: a
inputs.tooltip: A sequence, or a single value

inputs.name: b
inputs.tooltip: A sequence, or a single value

inputs.name: c
inputs.tooltip: A third sequence (optional)

nodes.description: Rows of values (a spreadsheet's Read range, or Table to Rows) as a table of named columns, the first row the names (without a header, c1, c2, …). A column is INT, FLOAT or BOOL when every value is one, else STRING. Table to Rows goes the other way.

inputs.name: rows
inputs.tooltip: Rows: a list of lists

inputs.name: header
inputs.tooltip: The first row holds the column names

nodes.description: A table (named columns, as Letter counts or Transients make it, or a 2-D table array, as Histogram makes it) as rows of values, the column names first: what a spreadsheet's Write range takes. Rows already in rows pass through.

inputs.name: table
inputs.tooltip: A table: {"columns": [{name, values}]}

inputs.name: header
inputs.tooltip: Put the column names first

nodes.description: A list of tuples (from Zip, Outer Join or Vary Range 2D's xy) split into its parts: a, b and c are lists that zip downstream, so the settings they feed vary together. A single tuple splits into single values.

inputs.name: tuples
inputs.tooltip: A list of tuples, or one tuple

nodes.description: The items of a, b (and c) paired up in order, as one list of tuples: (a1, b1), (a2, b2), … The lists must be the same length; a single value goes with every item. Unzip splits the tuples again.

inputs.name: a
inputs.tooltip: A sequence, or a single value

inputs.name: b
inputs.tooltip: A sequence, or a single value

inputs.name: c
inputs.tooltip: A third sequence (optional)

nodes.description: A list of on/off values to sweep a setting with: wire it into a parameter and that node runs once per value, each result labelled with its value. Several varied settings zip when they come from the same Vary node, and form every combination when they don't.

inputs.tooltip: The values, comma-separated; true/false, yes/no, on/off or 1/0

nodes.description: A list of numbers to sweep a setting with: wire it into a parameter and that node runs once per value, each result labelled with its value. Several varied settings zip when they come from the same Vary node, and form every combination when they don't.

inputs.name: values
inputs.tooltip: The values, comma-separated; a range as start:stop:step (stop included when the steps land on it; step 1 if left out) or start:stop/count (count values, evenly spaced, both ends included)

inputs.tooltip: The values, comma-separated; a range as start:stop:step (stop included when the steps land on it; step 1 if left out) or start:stop/count (count values, evenly spaced, both ends included)
